criteria.evidence: In the diff, planner.rs adds `pub deadline_s: u64` to PlannerInputs with a doc comment. It adds `pub(super) const DEADLINE_RULE`, whose doc comment says the planner's fixed wall-clock deadline was never stated to it and names both job ids. `planner_brief` writes `deadline_section(inputs.deadline_s)` before `## Report`, for every round.

criteria.criterion: The rule in the planner brief states the deadline in seconds and says that a planner killed at the deadline produces no plan. It tells the planner to sort its reading by what the criteria need, to stop exploring well before the deadline (the rule gives a fraction of the deadline), and to return the best complete plan it has, with unresolved items as `User:` or `Host:` open questions. Check with Grep on the constant in planner.rs.
criteria.evidence: I read the DEADLINE_RULE text. It contains: 'a deadline of {deadline_s} seconds'; 'A planner stopped at the deadline sends no plan'; 'Sort your reading by what the acceptance criteria need'; 'stop exploring by {stop_s} seconds (half the deadline)'; and 'Return the best complete plan you have, with anything unresolved as an open question beginning `User:` or `Host:`'. `deadline_section` fills in stop_s = deadline_s/2.

findings.summary: The live planner deadline is already 86400 s at the base commit, so this change mainly helps shorter configured deadlines, not the two original 600 s failures.
findings.evidence: athena.toml:224 reads `planner_timeout_s = 86400`. The evidence history.json shows commit 740a9e4, 'Raise stage time limits to 24 hours in athena.toml', dated 2026-11-14. The reading's code survey said '600 in athena.toml'. The CHANGELOG entry and the DEADLINE_RULE doc comment both state this, so nothing is hidden. The fix is still right for any configured deadline.

findings.summary: The rule is prose only. Whether planners follow it, or whether 'half the deadline' is the right point to stop, is not measured.
findings.evidence: The doc comment and CHANGELOG mark the rule as information, not enforcement, and call half the deadline an estimate. That meets the mechanism default. A later job could check planner wall times against the stated stop point.

findings.summary: For very small deadlines, `deadline_section` raises the stop figure to at least 1 with `.max(1)`, and no test covers that.
findings.evidence: `let stop_s = (deadline_s / 2).max(1);` For deadline_s = 1 the brief says stop by 1 second, which equals the deadline. This is harmless, since the config refuses 0.

summary: The change passes. It fixes the cause where it starts. Every planner brief, first round and revision alike, now has a `## Deadline` section. That section gives the deadline in seconds and says a planner stopped at the deadline sends no plan. It says the planner has no clock and should count its tool calls against a reading order. It says to stop exploring by half the deadline and to return the best complete plan, with unresolved items as `User:` or `Host:` open questions. The figure comes from `cfg.planner_timeout_s`, the same value planning.rs:163 passes to `agent_spec`, so the deadline shown cannot differ from the one enforced. I ran the new unit test and the whole athena-context suite (158 passed), and the new athena-core run test, which passed for both 600 and 4321. Athena's revert runs show both new tests fail without the fix. The CI record shows fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed. Only the five expected files changed, and no refusal rule was added. One fact to know: athena.toml at the base commit already sets `planner_timeout_s = 86400`, through commit 740a9e4, which I confirmed in the evidence history.json. The reading's survey said 600. The CHANGELOG states the 86400 value honestly, so the two original 600 s failures are mainly prevented for shorter configured deadlines. Whether planners follow the rule is not measured, and the change says so.
